text:
Colorado arrives rested and rolling after a 4-0 win over Detroit, where projected starter Mackenzie Blackwood stopped all 27 shots. The Avalanche are 3-1-1 in their last five, without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. Toronto is 1-4-0 in that span and winless in three, shut out 4-0 by New Jersey two days ago, with Kirill Marchenko on injured reserve. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Paul and Nylander, and Jack Roslovic has moved onto the first power-play unit. Nicolas Roy also returns to Toronto for the first time since leaving the Maple Leafs.

Our numbers favor Colorado, 3.41 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 2.81. At five on five, the Avalanche have taken 53% of the expected goals in their games and the Maple Leafs 46%. The special teams matchup to watch is Colorado's power play, which creates 0.80 expected goals a game, against a Toronto penalty kill that allows 0.80. Toronto also takes 4.4 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Blackwood (+1.6 goals saved above expected, meaning goals prevented beyond what the shots warranted) and Sergei Bobrovsky (+0.6) are close this season. Bobrovsky was 13.5 below expected last year and is .862 over his last five starts.

Nathan MacKinnon is 42% to score and 87% for a point. For Toronto, Auston Matthews is 38% to score and William Nylander 36%. Our under-the-radar picks are both Avalanche: Gabriel Landeskog, a third-liner with 2.4 expected goals over his last 10 games and a 20% chance to score, and T.J. Hughes, 43% for a point, above his season pace.
